rationale: PINS the swift `exports` surface (DERIV_EXPORTS_SWIFT4). Swift has no export KEYWORD; its export construct is ACCESS CONTROL, which the pinned grammar reduces to `modifiers > visibility_modifier` on declarations and on imports. Corpus measurement over the derived 24,386-file population (stride 8, 3,048 files) finds 28 `public import`, 29 `@_exported import`, 1,189 `public` nominals in 441 files, 5,073 `public` members in 667 files and 62 `open` nominals — so RULED was available and would have been wrong. Pins five shapes: (1) public/open on a FILE-SCOPE declaration is an export; (2) internal/private are not; (3) a public MEMBER of an internal type is NOT a module export, because Swift caps a member's access at its container's; (4) a re-exporting import (`public import`, `@_exported import`) is an export IN ADDITION to the `references` edge the same import already produces; (5) `public extension Array` does not export `Array` — it makes the extension's MEMBERS public, and Array is the stdlib's declaration. The source is the file's own leaf name (`exports-visibility`), the family spelling for a module-level edge endpoint (typescript moduleLeafName(), go packageName, python moduleName), NOT the literal `root` this analyzer uses for `references` — `root` is in parallel-indexer's SYMBOL_NAME_DENYLIST so an edge sourced there can never bind to a stored symbol, while an `exports` TARGET is a declaration in this very file and does bind. The `Decorated` export additionally pins the M59.A7 LINE rule: its declaration node starts on the `@available(...)` attribute's line (71) and its NAME node is on line 73, so the edge must carry 73 — a line a reader can check against the source — and never the decorator's. Mutant SW-EXP-14 injects exactly that substitution and must die on it.

expectRelationships.note: M59.A7 line contract: the DECLARATION node starts on the @available attribute's line (71); the NAME node is on 73, so the edge must carry 73 and never the decorator's.

forbidRelationships.comment: an `internal class` is the ABSENCE of an export, not one
a `private struct` is the ABSENCE of an export, not one
`public extension Array` makes the extension's MEMBERS public; Array is the stdlib's declaration, not this module's export
a public MEMBER of an internal type exports nothing — Swift caps a member's access at its container's, and the member is reachable through contains Hidden -> notAnExport
not public, and nested in a type — never a module-level export
a member of a public extension is not a module-level export either
a PLAIN `import Foundation` is a dependency (references), not a re-export — only `public import` / `@_exported import` export
the exports source is the file's leaf name, never the `root` literal — `root` is in parallel-indexer's SYMBOL_NAME_DENYLIST so an edge sourced there can never bind to a stored symbol
